implementerProof.how: Three of the implementer's four live proofs were driven again independently, on scratch pull requests of my own (sjawhar/legion #2565, #2566, #2567, #2568, #2569, #2570, all merged or closed and every scratch branch deleted), with the mutation text read out of the shipped packages/daemon/internal/ghautomerge/ghautomerge.go rather than copied from the handoff, and as the review App rather than the implement App: the merge's squash message (acceptance 2), the release level of both merges (D5), and the unit suite. Each reproduced the implementer's result. The fourth, GitHub accepting and storing the arm's headline and body on a protected base, could not be driven with my credential: enablePullRequestAutoMerge on sjawhar/legion#2562 as the review App is refused 'Pull request refusing to allow a GitHub App to create or update workflow `.github/workflows/pr-title.yaml` without `workflows` permission', since this pull request edits a workflow file and the review App holds no workflows: write. What I could read of it holds: GitHub's timeline of #2562 carries two AutoMergeDisabledEvent entries by legion-implementer at 17:42:45Z and 17:53:31Z, so the implementer did arm and disarm it as recorded, and #2562 is armed with nothing now (autoMergeRequest null, mergeQueueEntry null, read after my own refused attempt). GitHub's own schema confirms what the arm takes and the merge-queue limit the implementer recorded: EnablePullRequestAutoMergeInput's commitHeadline and commitBody each read 'if omitted, a default message will be used. NOTE: when merging with a merge queue any input value ... is ignored'.

proof.criterion: Acceptance 2: a merge driven through GitHub's API on a scratch sjawhar/legion pull request leaves a squash commit whose message has no Dispatch key, no Omp-Session line and no skip-checks line.
proof.surface: real GitHub, as the review App, with the shipped mergePullRequest text read out of packages/daemon/internal/ghautomerge/ghautomerge.go: a scratch base branch of main, a head of two commits whose messages carry a neutral project key (ACME-1), two Omp-Session: lines, a BREAKING CHANGE: footer and the skip-checks trailer, and a pull request of the head onto that base
proof.command: sed -n '/^\tmerge = `/,/^}`$/p' packages/daemon/internal/ghautomerge/ghautomerge.go | sed '1s/^[^`]*`//; $s/`$//' > merge-new.graphql; bash mkpr.sh a 'fix(scratch): the daemon-written squash message, read by the tester'; gh api graphql -f query="$(cat merge-new.graphql)" -F id=<node> -F head=58bb4f07e29669cd10e2a38647d7fa9c38b6e329 -f method=SQUASH -f headline='fix(scratch): the daemon-written squash message, read by the tester (#2565)' -f body=''; gh api repos/sjawhar/legion/git/commits/31085ad1ffa1916f5ddeedbacb910be031a0d75f --jq .message
proof.observed: sjawhar/legion#2565 merged as 31085ad1ffa1916f5ddeedbacb910be031a0d75f. Its whole commit message is 76 bytes on one line: 'fix(scratch): the daemon-written squash message, read by the tester (#2565)'. A grep of that message for Omp-Session, skip-checks, ACME-, BREAKING CHANGE, Co-authored-by and the '* ' bullet GitHub joins with found nothing. gh run list on the scratch head returned 0 runs, so the proof started no workflow. The repository's live settings make this the real default: squash_merge_commit_message=COMMIT_MESSAGES, squash_merge_commit_title=COMMIT_OR_PR_TITLE.
proof.negativeControl: The same mutation as it stood before this change (jj file show -r 73e5b3ab8c79 of the same file, no commitHeadline and no commitBody), on scratch pull request #2566 built from branch commits identical in shape, merged as 013168af4398f0c298ac81b51ced520c9bca17dc: its message carries the joined default body - both branch commit subjects as '* ' bullets, both Omp-Session: lines, the skip-checks: true line, the BREAKING CHANGE: footer, the ACME-1 key and a Co-authored-by: trailer (5 leak lines matched). That is the live defect this change removes, reproduced at the same head.

proof.criterion: Acceptance 1: a unit test of ghautomerge shows both mutations sending the headline and the body, and the body holds no commit message of the pull request.
proof.surface: the Go unit suite of packages/daemon/internal/ghautomerge, whose fake records what each mutation's input actually passes rather than what the variables map holds, plus the daemon's own READY-merge tests
proof.observed: ok github.com/sjawhar/legion/daemon/internal/ghautomerge 0.171s; ok github.com/sjawhar/legion/daemon/internal/daemon 0.094s. The submission table asserts headline="<title> (#42)" body="" for the merge-queue enqueue, for the auto-merge arm and for the two immediate merges, and one row whose fake answers a title of its own asserts the headline carries that title rather than the default. (internal/daemon runs in this pod only with GOWORK left at the repository's go.work; with GOWORK=off it fails to build on testnats, which is the pod, not the branch.)
proof.negativeControl: Dropping title from the read query's pull-request selection (id state title headRefOid -> id state headRefOid) leaves the suite GREEN at the implementer's head - the fake answered a title the query no longer asked for. With the lock this phase adds, the same mutant fails five submission rows with headline=" (#42)", and the shipped code stays green. That mutant's effect on GitHub was measured too, below.

proof.criterion: D5: an empty body makes the release level of a daemon-merged commit title-only, which is what the three prose corrections state.
proof.surface: .github/scripts/release-bump.sh, run in a throwaway shallow clone of the two scratch base branches under $TMPDIR, over the two merges above
proof.command: git clone --depth 2 --branch scratch/infra-825-t-a-base --single-branch https://github.com/sjawhar/legion.git bumpa && cd bumpa && git fetch --depth 2 origin scratch/infra-825-t-b-base && bash .github/scripts/release-bump.sh 1.0.0 "$(git rev-parse <merge>^1)..<merge>" -- .scratch-infra-825
proof.observed: The daemon-written merge 31085ad1 (body: 0 lines) printed 1.0.1 - the patch its 'fix(scratch):' title earns. The GitHub-default merge 013168af (body: 10 lines), from branch commits identical but for the pull request title, printed 2.0.0 - the major bump the BREAKING CHANGE: footer earned through the joined body. So the breaking footer in a branch commit body no longer reaches the release level through a daemon merge, exactly as release-bump.sh's new header, pr-title.yaml's message and the AGENTS.md sentence now say. (The implementer measured none against 2.0.0 because its scratch title was a non-releasing chore:; mine was a fix:, so the title-only level is 1.0.1. Same conclusion, read through a releasing title.)
proof.negativeControl: The GitHub-default merge is the control: the same two branch commits, the same path filter, the same range shape, and a different token (2.0.0 against 1.0.1), so the answer reflects the squash body and not the range or the filter.

proof.criterion: The headline survives GitHub unchanged: GitHub appends no second (#n), truncates no long title, and alters no character of one.
proof.surface: real GitHub, the shipped mergePullRequest on scratch pull request #2567, whose title is 234 characters and carries double quotes, a backtick span, a percent, a dollar, a #1234 reference and a trailing (#9999)
proof.command: gh api graphql -f query="$(cat merge-new.graphql)" -F id=<node> -F head=2086dab18db008d1e6a21762bca321e1d97d8b73 -f method=SQUASH -f headline='<the 242-character headline>' -f body=''
proof.observed: Merge commit dd56b30c95d5b3e564fc7a32d342aa82e61f59c3, whose message is 242 bytes on one line and byte-for-byte the headline sent, trailing '(#9999) (#2567)' included: GitHub appended no number of its own, truncated nothing, and escaped nothing.
proof.negativeControl: The same mutation with headline='' and body='' on scratch pull request #2568 merged as 77ebcd59e69460199ef32e729d96785dd84c8901, whose message is GitHub's own default title, 'fix(scratch): the refusals the tester drives against the shipped mutations (#2568)', with no body. So GitHub reads an empty headline as an omission and an empty body as a value - which is the measurement F4 said the whole change rests on, taken from the other side.

triedToBreakIt: A head that moved between the daemon's read and its mutation. The mutation sent with a real but superseded head is refused by GitHub, 'Head branch was modified. Review and try the merge again.' (scratch #2569 at its old head after a third commit), which is the error packages/daemon/internal/daemon/auto_merge_test.go:181 already names, so Submit's refusal path is reached and nothing merges. An all-zeros expectedHeadOid instead answers HTTP 200 with the 13-byte body {"data":null} and no errors array, which githubrest.Client.GraphQL reads as success and Submit would report Merged; that input is unreachable, since Submit sends only the head GitHub reported open at (pull.openAt(head)), so it is no defect, and it is recorded because the next reader of that switch should not have to measure it again.

A merge of a pull request whose head is already merged: the mutation answers {"data":null} too, and Submit never reaches it, returning Already from the read (pull.State == MERGED && HeadRefOid == head).

The arm on a base with no ruleset: GitHub refuses it on every state a scratch base reaches. My own run met 'Pull request Pull request is in clean status' on a clean scratch pull request, beside the three refusals the implementer recorded. No scratch harness can drive the arm, and adding a ruleset needs administration: write, which neither role App holds.

testGapFixed.gap: The package's fake answered the read's title whatever the read query selected, so the read side had none of the discipline the implementer built for the mutation side (passed(), which records a field the mutation's input leaves out as <absent>). Measured: deleting title from the read query's pull-request selection left the whole suite green at the implementer's head.
testGapFixed.consequence: Measured on real GitHub, not inferred: with no title in the read, Submit builds the headline ' (#<n>)' from an empty pull.Title, and GitHub accepts it and writes exactly that as the squash subject - scratch pull request #2570 merged as 3d84aee8c012981eda92f86b59d7bdd795473093, whose whole commit message is ' (#2570)'. A future edit to that one line of the query would put a subject like that on the default branch with CI green.
testGapFixed.fix: Commit 9965a1e792fb, test(daemon): the ghautomerge fake answers a title only while the read selects it. The fake now answers the title field only while the query asks for it, as GitHub does. The shipped code stays green; the same mutant now fails five submission rows with headline=" (#42)". It is a regression lock, not proof of a criterion, and it changes no production file.

notProven: The merge GitHub makes later from a stored auto-merge arm. GitHub accepting the arm with this change's headline and empty body, and storing both, is the implementer's recorded run on sjawhar/legion#2562 (its disarms are on GitHub's timeline); driving that arm through to a merge would mean merging a real pull request on a protected base, and no scratch base can be protected without administration: write. The pull request body records it under Not proven / risk.

A merge-queue base, where GitHub's schema says both inputs are ignored. sjawhar/legion's main carries no merge-queue rule, so no surface here reaches it; the other repository the project serves is private.
